draft.title: Language and culture
card: A language is more than a set of words. It carries the ideas, values and ways of seeing the world that a cultural group shares.

The words a language has can show what a culture pays attention to. Many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages have detailed words for kin relationships, which show how much weight those relationships carry.
Some words cannot be translated directly into another language with a single word. The Danish word hygge, a cosy feeling of comfort and togetherness, needs a whole sentence in English.
When a language is lost, the ideas and knowledge held in its words can be lost too. This is why many communities work to keep their languages alive.
draft.remember: Language holds a culture's ideas and values, so some words do not translate neatly.

a.q: Why is it hard to translate hygge into English with one word?
opts: It names an idea that English has no single word for
It is a word that only young Danish people use
It has no meaning outside the country of Denmark
It is spelt in a way that English cannot write
a.why: Hygge carries a Danish idea about comfort and togetherness, and English has no single word for it. It can still be explained in a sentence, so it is not meaningless outside Denmark.
a.clue: Think about what the word carries, not how it is spelt.

b.q: Sam moves to a new school and learns that his classmates' language has many words for kin relationships. What does this best suggest about their culture?
opts: Kin relationships carry great weight in their culture
Their culture has no use for other kinds of words
Their language is simpler than other languages
Their culture has not changed over time
b.why: Detailed words for a topic can show that a culture pays close attention to it. The other options claim more than the words show, and none of them follows from having many kin terms.
b.clue: Detailed words can show what a culture pays attention to.

a.best: It names an idea that English has no single word for

b.best: Kin relationships carry great weight in their culture

b.q: Lena studies the language of a coastal community. It has many separate words for different tides and kinds of waves. What does this best suggest?
opts: The sea matters a great deal in the community's life
The community's language is simpler than most others
The community's culture has not changed in a long time
The community has little interest in life on the land
b.why: Detailed words for a topic can show that a culture pays close attention to it, so many words for tides and waves suggest the sea matters to this community. Having many sea words does not show a lack of interest in the land: the words show what a culture focuses on, not what it ignores.
b.clue: Ask what detailed words show about a culture's attention.
